questions.title: Why does QLoRA’s NF4 data type provide better performance than simple 4-bit integer quantization?
questions.question_body: In the QLoRA paper, the authors claim that using a 4‑bit NormalFloat (NF4) data type yields better empirical performance than 4‑bit integers or 4‑bit floats. I understand that NF4 is information‑theoretically optimal for normally distributed data, but could someone explain how this theoretical property translates into reduced quantization error in practice? Specifically, how does the bin allocation in NF4 differ from that of uniform int4 or float4, and why does this matter for transformer weight distributions?

questions.title: How does Double Quantization reduce the memory footprint of blockwise scaling constants?
questions.question_body: The paper introduces Double Quantization (DQ), where the first quantization layer produces per‑block scaling constants $c_2$ that are themselves quantized to 8‑bit floats with a larger blocksize. I’d like a step‑by‑step explanation of the memory savings: starting from a standard blocksize of 64 with 32‑bit FP32 scales, how do we compute the average bits per parameter after performing a second quantization with blocksize 256? Also, why is subtracting the mean from $c_2$ before quantization useful?

questions.title: What is the role of Paged Optimizers in preventing GPU out‑of‑memory during QLoRA training?
questions.question_body: QLoRA uses NVIDIA unified memory to page optimizer states between CPU RAM and GPU when training hits memory spikes caused by gradient checkpointing. Could someone clarify which parts of the optimizer state are paged (e.g., Adam moment estimates), how often paging occurs during typical training on a 48GB GPU with a minibatch size of 16, and whether this introduces any latency or correctness issues compared to keeping all optimizer states resident on GPU?

questions.title: Why is it necessary to add LoRA adapters to *every* transformer block to match full finetuning performance?
questions.question_body: Figure 2 in the paper shows that limiting LoRA adapters to only query/value matrices or to a subset of layers leads to significant accuracy loss. Intuitively, why would attaching adapters to every linear layer restore full finetuning performance? Is it because gradients must flow through all frozen weights for effective specialization, or are there other interactions (e.g., residual connections) that necessitate full coverage?

questions.title: How does QLoRA recover lost precision when fine‑tuning a quantized base?
questions.question_body: "We show that NF4 + LoRA recovers full‑precision performance when finetuning a 4‑bit model". What mechanisms allow LoRA training through fixed 4‑bit weights to reverse the degradation that occurs when simply finetuning a quantized model? Do we view the adapters as performing a corrective projection in parameter space, or does back‑propagating through the frozen weights change their effective representation during training?

questions.title: What are the limitations of using GPT‑4 as an automated evaluator in chatbot benchmarks?
questions.question_body: The authors mention order effects and lower inter‑rater agreement between GPT‑4 and humans when comparing model responses. Could someone elaborate on why GPT‑4 might favor responses appearing earlier in its prompt, and what statistical measures (e.g., Fleiss κ) indicate about its consistency? How might these biases impact Elo rating calculations based on GPT‑4 judgments?

questions.title: Can QLoRA be extended to support other PEFT methods beyond LoRA?
questions.question_body: "We leave it to future work to explore tradeoffs of other PEFT approaches." Suppose we wanted to use prefix tuning or adapter prompt mixing instead of LoRA. What changes would be required in the double–dequantization step and memory budget calculations? Are there inherent benefits or obstacles specific to each method when combined with blockwise 4‑bit quantization?

questions.title: Why does SOTA instruction fine‑tuning datasets differ so much in their impact on MMLU vs chatbot benchmarks?
questions.question_body: "Training LLaMA on FLAN v2 performs well on MMLU but poorly on Vicuna". Can someone explain conceptually why two datasets that both claim to enable instruction following can drive performance trends in such divergent ways? Does this reflect differences in content style, length distribution, or prompt structure?
